newsitem.title: USA: Cohen looks for new Pentagon number two.
newsitem.headline: Cohen looks for new Pentagon number two.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen said on Thursday he will look within and outside the Pentagon for candidates to replace Deputy Secretary John White, who will leave the Defence Department's number two job in June.

"We obviously (will) look for somebody who is familiar with defence issues, is familiar with management techniques and responsibilities, someone who is highly regarded by those in the Pentagon and Capitol Hill," Cohen told reporters.

"We will look for the most qualified individuals. It could come from within the Pentagon. But we will look at all candidates," he said in response to questions at a news conference with Ukrainian Defence Minister Olexander Kuzmuk.
Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon said earlier in the day that White, 60, would leave to return to private life after two years on the job.

Bacon said that Cohen would move as quickly as possible to replace White, a former business executive and defence analyst. But he also said Cohen was now concentrating on a sweeping review of U.S. security policy and force structure.

The Washington Post reported on Thursday that White, a former business executive and an assistant defence secretary under former President Jimmy Carter, informed Cohen he would leave this summer after remaining long enough to help out in the so-called Quadrennial Defence Review.

White, 60, agreed when Cohen replaced William Perry as secretary in February that he would stay for at least several months to assist in a smooth transition and to work on the QDR, which will result in major decisions on arms modernisation and force structure.
The QDR report is due to be sent to Congress on May 15.
"We are now at the end of a very successful transition," White said in a letter to Cohen released by the Pentagon. "The time has now come for me to move on to new challenges."
The Post reported that White had no firm idea of what he wanted to do next.

White, a former vice president of Eastman Kodak Co., was named by Perry to become deputy secretary after heading a blue-ribbon panel of military and private experts on streamlining the armed forces. He is considered a skilled administrator.
